notes: Sweep 2026-10-31-b (result.json head 74112b4, uncommitted false): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). All have rc 0 and a model_id matching the requested model; every assistant message in each transcript names that model. reads is empty in all five. skills_listed is 209 in every run, as in the previous sweep. haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 made a single Write call; haiku-2 made a Write and an Edit; opus-1 wrote the file, then checked it against a stub Req with Bash and removed its check files.

git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes none of the eleven listed rules. It changes two rules outside the list (One expression per line, and the do: rule, both about `for`), macros.md and an example in processes.md. No run uses a `for`, a macro or a process, so those changes decide nothing here. All eleven rules are graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/library-client-baseline.json: an option value reaching Req or a String function unchecked violates Make polymorphism explicit; options not checked with Keyword.validate!/2, or ## Options outside the function's @doc, violate Group related parameters; a key held only in a bare Req request or a plain map leaves Keep secrets not exercised; message/1 under @impl needs no @spec.

In multi-clause functions: the deciding sentence is "A field no pattern or guard uses makes the reader scan every head to find what selects when the same field is bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or when it is bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines". Two runs have a function of three or more clauses. sonnet-1 handle_response/1 binds body in two of three heads (lines 149, 165); opus-1 handle_response/1 binds body-only fields in one of four (line 187). In both, the {:error, exception} clause binds neither, so no field is bound in every clause, and both are clean. This differs from haiku-1 of the previous sweep, whose third clause also bound body. Haiku turns clean because neither Haiku run has a function of three or more clauses this time.

Make polymorphism explicit: the deciding sentence is "An option value needs the same check as a positional argument: `Keyword.validate!/2` checks the keys, not the values, so an `api_key` taken from `opts` and put straight into a request header is unchecked input." All five runs are violated. haiku-2 line 77 rejects nil and "" but no other non-binary, so its key is unchecked too. haiku-1 and haiku-2 check coordinates in a private validate_coordinates/2 that returns an error tuple and not with a guard; I counted that as a check, since a bad coordinate still stops in WeatherClient before Req.

Keep secrets: the deciding sentence is "When a struct holds credentials, derive `Inspect` without them, so they do not appear in logs, crash reports, or IEx output". sonnet-2 is violated because it defines a struct holding the Req request (line 23) with no derive. sonnet-1 keeps the same request bare, with no struct of its own, so it is not exercised under the standard above, while the case's inspect check is missed for both. The Sonnet tier turns violated through sonnet-2.

Other tier changes against the previous sweep come from the runs, not the rules. Sonnet turns clean on Read required keys because no run reads response keys with brackets. Sonnet turns violated on Take configuration through sonnet-1's Application.get_env fallbacks. Haiku turns clean on Use exception structs because both Haiku runs define a defexception error. Group related parameters stays Opus clean, Haiku and Sonnet violated: sonnet-1 passes and sonnet-2 breaks it.

Other violations follow the previous sweep's standard. Match every expected shape is flagged for sonnet-1 (status catch-all against its Error doc), for opus-1 (a 201 with a valid forecast reported as not a forecast; narrow, since the API description only implies 200) and for haiku-2 (catch-alls that hide Jason's error). haiku-2 also has a one-step pipeline, an else block, a case nested in a with and fetch_option/3 returning a bare value. haiku-1's Forecast struct is flagged under Parse external data, whose text says "Define structs with `@enforce_keys` for the required fields and a `@type t`."; the previous sweep had no such case to compare with.

Formatting rechecked with mix format --check-formatted in the scratch folder and matches result.json format_ok: opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 pass; sonnet-1 fails at line 149; sonnet-2 fails at lines 62 and 89. Compile results recorded in result.json were confirmed against a stub Req and are not graded: opus-1 and sonnet-1 compile; haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 do not, because WeatherClient builds %Error{} before the file defines WeatherClient.Error.
Expected reads (library-design.md) is unmet in every run, as expected for baseline.
